semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Online continual learning is a nuanced subcategory of continual learning, where the learning algorithm is exposed to incoming data streams. While the 'online' aspect differentiates it slightly, it still fundamentally falls under continual learning.
Online continual learning involves aspects of online learning, where learning happens in real-time as data becomes available.

parent_domains.justification: Online continual learning is a specialized area within the broader scope of continual learning.
Online continual learning inherently involves online learning aspects, as it deals with real-time or sequential data processes.
Incremental learning is a parent domain because online continual learning incrementally updates models with new data over time.
Lifelong learning is a broad concept that encompasses ongoing learning processes, including online continual learning.

closest_parent_domain.justification: While online continual learning involves aspects of online and incremental learning, it is most closely related to continual learning since its primary focus is on the continual adaptation and learning over time with incoming data.

child_domains.justification: No-regret online learning can be a sub-domain as it emphasizes making sequence decisions with minimal long-term loss, aligning with continual online adaptation.
Online meta-learning can be a child domain because it involves meta-learning processes applied in real-time sequences, akin to online continual learning.

closest_child_domain.justification: Online meta-learning most closely aligns with online continual learning due to its emphasis on learning-to-learn in dynamic and real-time environments.

sibling_domains.justification: Both online reinforcement learning and online continual learning operate in real-time settings, focusing on adapting to new information immediately.
Both class-incremental learning and online continual learning involve the incremental adaptation of models through new data classes or streams.
Online active learning is a sibling domain because it also involves making decisions on-the-fly about which data to learn from next, similar to online continual learning.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Online reinforcement learning is the closest sibling domain because, like online continual learning, it focuses on immediate, adaptive decision-making in dynamic environments.

unrelated_domains.justification: Although related to continual learning, catastrophic forgetting is more of a challenge within the domain rather than a domain itself.
Dynamic learning can apply to various types of learning systems and does not specifically relate to online continual adaptation.
Offline learning contrasts with online continual learning as it involves batch processing of data, rather than real-time adaptation.
Distributed learning involves partitioning data and computation across multiple systems, not specifically focusing on the online, continual nature of learning.
While beneficial, communication-efficient learning is more about reducing communication costs in distributed settings rather than focusing on continual, online learning.
This domain is fundamentally different as it uses pre-recorded data for reinforcement learning tasks, which is contrary to online continual learning principles.
Similar to distributed learning, it focuses on training across distributed systems rather than the continual learning aspect.
Although related to ongoing adaptation, continuous control learning is more specific to control systems rather than general continual learning.
Cooperative learning involves collaborative approaches, which may not directly align with the individual, ongoing learning focus of online continual learning.
Like catastrophic forgetting, this is more of an issue faced within learning processes rather than a distinct domain.
